items.q: What is an AI phone assistant?
items.a: An AI phone assistant is a digital assistant that answers the phone for your business, with a human-like voice. You will also hear AI receptionist: it is the same thing. She answers questions about your business, books appointments in your calendar and puts the call through to you when needed. After every call, a summary is in your CRM.

items.q: Can a caller tell they're talking to AI?
items.a: Yes. You choose how she introduces herself: for example as your business's digital assistant, as in the examples on this page. Whatever your greeting sounds like, we set her up so the caller knows they are talking to an AI assistant. That is also what the European AI Act requires: anyone talking to AI must know it. So the caller knows where they stand, even though she has a human-like voice.

items.q: What does an AI receptionist cost?
items.a: €750 one-off and €150 a month, as an add-on to the Online Growth package (€150 a month, cancellable monthly). The monthly price includes 300 call minutes; each extra minute costs €0.35. All prices excl. VAT.

items.q: Does it work on my existing number?
items.a: Yes. We set up call forwarding on your current number. Your customers just call you as they always do.

items.q: What if she doesn't know the answer?
items.a: If she doesn't know the answer, she puts the caller through to you. If you don't pick up, she has already noted the question and let you know, so you can call back. We set her up not to guess: when in doubt, it comes to you.

items.q: Will she understand my customers, even with an accent?
items.a: You test that yourself: before she goes live, you call her first. If she doesn't catch something, she asks again or puts the call through. Whatever doesn't go well, we fine-tune.

items.q: Can she put appointments in my calendar?
items.a: In a regular calendar, yes: she suggests free slots, books the appointment and the caller gets a confirmation by SMS. If you work with a service menu, she can't book in it herself yet. She then texts the caller the link to book themselves.

items.q: Which businesses is an AI phone assistant suitable for?
items.a: For businesses that work with appointments and often get calls while you are busy with a customer: a hair salon, a beauty salon, a practice or a garage, for example. What she does in each of those, you can read in the sector blocks on this page.
The transcript and a short summary go into your CRM. That way you can read later who called and what was arranged.

items.q: Do I hear her real voice on this page?
items.a: No. With the sound on, you hear your own device's built-in reading voice, and that sounds different on every device. Your receptionist herself has a human-like voice.

sectoren.h2a: An AI phone assistant for your business.
sectoren.lede: In a hair salon she gets different questions than in a garage. That is why we set her up for your business: your services, your calendar and what she leaves to you. This is what that can look like.

items.label: Hair salon
items.h: You cut. She answers the phone.
items.q: Can I still come in on Saturday for a colour and a cut?
do: With a regular calendar, she tells the caller which slots are free and books the appointment. With a service menu, where your customer picks the stylist and the treatment, she texts them the link.
She answers questions about your prices and opening hours, as they are on your website.
Someone wants to move or cancel an appointment? She notes it down and lets you know. You make the change.

link.t: Website for hair salons with online booking (in Dutch)

items.label: Beauty salon
items.h: You are with a client. She answers the questions.
items.q: How long does a facial take, and what does it cost?
do: She explains what a treatment involves, how long it takes and what it costs, as you put it on your website or in your price list.
With a regular calendar, she books the treatment and the client gets a confirmation by text. With a service menu, she texts the link to book online.
A question that needs your advice, such as a skin problem, she leaves to you: she puts the call through or notes the question for you.

items.label: Practice
items.h: You are with a patient. She takes the phone.
items.q: Do you still have room next week for a first consultation?
do: With a regular calendar, she books the consultation and the patient gets a confirmation by text. With a service menu, she texts the link to book online.
She answers practical questions, such as your address, your hours or what a patient should bring, if you put that in her information.
She does not give medical advice. If someone asks for it, she puts the call through to you or notes the question for you.

items.label: Garage
items.h: You are under a car. She books the service.
items.q: My car is due for a service. When can I bring it in?
do: She asks what you need to know, such as the make and the number plate, and adds it to the customer in your CRM.
She books the service or the tyre change in your calendar, with a confirmation by text.
Someone asks whether their car is ready? She does not know that. She puts the call through to you, or notes the question and lets you know.
